description:
Write Rust tests verifying that trust anchor NC seeding works correctly end-to-end.

**What:** Integration tests covering: valid leaf passes anchor NC; violating leaf fails; excluded leaf fails; malformed anchor NC DER surfaces an error via TryFrom.

**Algorithm (one test file pkix-path/tests/anchor_nc_tests.rs):**

Helper: load DER bytes from pkix-path/tests/fixtures/anchor-nc/<name>.der.

Tests:
1. test_anchor_nc_permitted_valid_leaf:
   - Load anchor-nc-permitted-dns CA cert → TrustAnchor::from_cert(...)
   - Load leaf-good-dns cert (SAN=good.example.com)
   - Call validate_path(&[leaf], &[anchor], policy, &DefaultVerifier::default())
   - Assert Ok — PKITS_NOW timestamp (2020-01-01)
   - Oracle: pyca generated the leaf within .example.com; our NC check must accept it.

2. test_anchor_nc_permitted_violating_leaf:
   - Same anchor, load leaf-evil-dns cert (SAN=evil.other.com)
   - Assert Err(Error::NameConstraintViolation { index: 0 })
   - Oracle: evil.other.com is not within .example.com per RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10.

3. test_anchor_nc_excluded_leaf:
   - Load anchor-nc-excluded-dns CA cert → TrustAnchor::from_cert(...)
   - Load leaf-excluded-dns cert (SAN=bad.example.com)
   - Assert Err(Error::NameConstraintViolation { index: 0 })
   - Oracle: bad.example.com is within the excluded subtree .example.com.

4. test_anchor_try_from_cert_malformed_nc:
   - Construct a Certificate whose NC extension value is invalid DER bytes (e.g., 0xFF 0xFF)
   - TrustAnchor::try_from(cert) → assert Err(Error::Der(_))
   - Oracle: the DER bytes 0xFFFF are invalid per DER spec; try_find_cert_ext must surface this.

5. test_anchor_from_cert_malformed_nc_silent:
   - Same malformed cert as test 4
   - TrustAnchor::from_cert(cert) → assert name_constraints == None (silently dropped)
   - Oracle: find_cert_ext converts decode error to None.

**Defensive programming rules:**
- All fixtures loaded from committed DER files — no inline cert generation.
- No test derives expected behavior from the code under test.
- Test 4 constructs the malformed cert programmatically (not from a file) since it is testing error handling of our own code.

**Note on test 4/5:** to construct a Certificate with a malformed NC extension, use x509_cert builders or manipulate a valid cert's extension bytes directly. The test must build the cert in a way that pkix-path can parse the outer Certificate structure but finds malformed bytes in the NC extension value.
title: Tests: anchor NC enforcement — permitted, excluded, malformed
